en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Twelfth Chapter
Regarding the Discourse on the One Who Has Seven More Births at Most:
Is a person who has seven more births at most one who is fixed in destiny after seven more births at most?
Yes, he is.
The mother was deprived of life...
the father was deprived of life...
an Arhat was deprived of life...
"Did you draw blood from a Tathāgata with a malicious mind...
or did you cause a schism in the Saṅgha?
"One should not say so... [and so forth].
Is a person who is "limited to seven births" one who is fixed as being limited to seven births?
Yes. Is he incapable of realizing the Dhamma in the interval? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one incapable of realizing the Dhamma in the interval? Yes.
The mother was deprived of life...
the father was deprived of life...
an Arhat was deprived of life...
"Did you draw blood from a Tathāgata with a malicious mind...
did you cause a schism in the Saṅgha?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
Is a person who is "seven-times-at-most" one who is fixed as seven-times-at-most?
Yes. Is there that fixed rule by which a person who is seven-times-at-most is fixed as seven-times-at-most? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … there are for you the foundations of mindfulness … [as before] … the right efforts …
The bases of psychic power … the faculties … the powers …
Are the factors of enlightenment those very factors by which a person who is "limited to seven more births" is determined as being "limited to seven more births"?
You should not say so... [etc.
...Is there no such determination by which a person who is "limited to seven more births" is determined as being "limited to seven more births"?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If there is no such fixed rule by which a person who is ‘seven-times-at-most’ is fixed as being seven-times-at-most, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘A person who is seven-times-at-most is fixed as being seven-times-at-most.’”
"You have no foundations of mindfulness...
nor factors of enlightenment, by means of which factors of enlightenment a person who is at most seven times reborn is fixed as one who is destined for seven more births at most"?
"Yes."

If you do not possess those factors of enlightenment by means of which a person who is "limited to seven more births" is destined for the state of being limited to seven more births, then indeed, it should not be said:
"A person limited to seven more births is destined for the state of being limited to seven more births.
Is it the case that a person limited to seven more births is destined for the state of being limited to seven more births?
“Yes.
“Is it by the rule of a once-returner?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
"Is it by way of the certainty of non-returning?
"One should not say so …pe… Is it by way of the certainty of arahantship?"
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … By what certainty?
By the certainty of stream-entry (sotāpatti-niyāma).
Is a person who is "limited to seven more births" one who is fixed as being limited to seven more births?
Yes. Are all those who enter the fixed course of stream-entry fixed as being limited to seven more births? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said:
“A person who is limited to seven more births is fixed in the state of being limited to seven more births”?
“Yes.
“But is he not one who has seven births at most?
“Yes.”
If he is one who has seven births at most, then indeed, O sir, it must be said:
"A person who has seven births at most is destined for the state of having seven births at most.
The Discussion on One Who Has Seven Births at Most is finished.
